title: Act on Fire Investigations by Fire Authorities
full_text:
ACT ON FIRE INVESTIGATIONS BY FIRE AUTHORITIES

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters necessary for scientific and professional investigations into the causes of fires, fire growth and spread, damage, and other matters, for use in fire prevention and firefighting policy.

Article 2 (Definitions)
(1) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. “Fire” means a combustion phenomenon that occurs contrary to a person’s intention or intentionally or negligently and requires extinguishment, or a chemical explosion that occurs or expands contrary to a person’s intention;
2. “Fire investigation” means a series of acts performed by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, the head of a fire headquarters, or the chief of a fire station to ascertain the cause of a fire, damage, response activities, and other matters, including collecting materials, questioning interested persons, etc., inspecting the scene, conducting examinations and expert appraisals, and performing experiments;
3. “Fire investigator” means a firefighting official who conducts fire investigations and whose expertise in fire investigation has been recognized;
4. “Interested persons, etc.” means the owner, manager, or occupant of an object of fire protection where a fire has occurred (hereinafter referred to as an “interested person”) and the following persons:
(a) A person who discovered and reported the fire scene;
(b) A person who witnessed the fire scene;
(c) A person who carried out firefighting activities or was involved in rescue activities, including guiding evacuation;
(d) A person who caused the fire or was connected with its occurrence.
(2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), the meanings of terms used in this Act shall be as prescribed in the Framework Act on Firefighting Services and the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Firefighting Systems.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the State, etc.)
(1) The State and local governments shall devise and implement measures for the research and development of technologies necessary for fire investigations and for improving the accuracy of fire investigations.
(2) Interested persons, etc. shall cooperate to ensure that fire investigations are conducted appropriately.

Article 4 (Relationship with Other Acts)
Except as otherwise specifically provided in other Acts, fire investigations shall be governed by this Act.

CHAPTER II CONDUCT OF FIRE INVESTIGATIONS, ETC.

Article 5 (Conduct of Fire Investigations)
(1) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, the head of a fire headquarters, or the chief of a fire station (hereinafter referred to as the “head of a fire authority”) shall conduct a fire investigation without delay upon learning that a fire has occurred. In such cases, the investigation shall not interfere with criminal investigations conducted by investigative agencies.
(2) When conducting a fire investigation under paragraph (1), the head of a fire authority shall investigate the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the cause of the fire;
2. Casualties and property damage caused by the fire;
3. Matters concerning response activities;
4. Matters concerning the installation, management, and operation of firefighting systems, etc.;
5. Matters concerning buildings and structures in which fires have occurred, fire risks by type of fire, and related matters;
6. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Matters necessary for the scope, procedures, etc. of fire investigations under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Establishment and Operation, etc. of Departments Dedicated to Fire Investigations)
(1) The head of a fire authority shall establish and operate a department dedicated to fire investigations (hereinafter referred to as a “dedicated department”) to conduct fire investigations based on professional expertise.
(2) A dedicated department shall perform the following duties:
1. Conducting fire investigations and analyzing and managing investigation results;
2. Developing technologies related to fire investigations and enhancing the capabilities of fire investigators;
3. Managing and operating facilities and equipment necessary for fire investigations;
4. Other duties necessary for fire investigations.
(3) The head of a fire authority shall have fire investigators perform fire investigation duties.
(4) Fire investigators shall be firefighting officials with professional qualifications in fire investigation, including firefighting officials who have passed the examination on fire investigation administered by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
(5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of dedicated departments, detailed qualification standards for fire investigators, their education and training, and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Formation and Operation of Joint Fire Investigation Teams)
(1) Where a large-scale fire or other fire prescribed by Presidential Decree occurs, such as a fire involving numerous casualties or attracting public attention, the head of a fire authority may form and operate a joint fire investigation team that includes relevant agencies and experts to conduct a comprehensive and detailed fire investigation.
(2) Matters necessary for the formation, operation, etc. of a joint fire investigation team under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Preservation of Fire Scenes, etc.)
(1) To the extent necessary for a fire investigation, the head of a fire authority may take measures to preserve the fire scene or designate the fire scene and its surrounding area as a controlled area: Provided, That where the fire is subject to investigation on suspicion of arson or negligent causing of fire, the chief of the competent police station or coast guard station (hereinafter referred to as the “police station chief”) shall designate the controlled area.
(2) No person shall enter a controlled area designated under paragraph (1) without permission from the head of a fire authority or the police station chief.
(3) Where measures to preserve a fire scene have been taken or a controlled area has been designated under paragraph (1), no person shall move, alter, or damage objects or other things at the fire scene without permission from the head of a fire authority or the police station chief: Provided, That this shall not apply where it is deemed that the public interest is significantly affected or where there are urgent grounds, such as rescuing persons.
(4) Matters necessary for measures to preserve fire scenes, the designation of controlled areas, access thereto, and related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9 (Entry and Investigation, etc.)
(1) Where necessary for a fire investigation, the head of a fire authority may order an interested person to submit a report or materials, have a fire investigator enter the relevant location to conduct a fire investigation, or have a fire investigator question interested persons, etc.
(2) A fire investigator conducting a fire investigation under Article 9 (1) shall carry identification evidencing the investigator's authority and present it to interested persons, etc.
(3) A fire investigator conducting a fire investigation under Article 9 (1) shall not interfere with the legitimate business of an interested person, use any secret learned while conducting the fire investigation for another purpose, or disclose any such secret to another person.

Article 10 (Appearance of Interested Persons, etc.)
(1) Where a fire investigation is necessary, the head of a fire authority may require interested persons, etc. to appear at a fire authority and question them.
(2) Matters necessary concerning the appearance and questioning of interested persons, etc. under Article 10 (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Collection of Physical Evidence for Fire Investigations, etc.)
(1) Where necessary for a fire investigation, the head of a fire authority may collect physical evidence and conduct inspections, tests, analyses, etc. of it. However, physical evidence related to a criminal investigation may be collected in consultation with the head of the investigative agency.
(2) Where the head of an investigative agency has already arrested a suspect or seized physical evidence on suspicion of arson or negligent causing of fire, the head of a fire authority may, if necessary for a fire investigation, investigate the suspect or the seized physical evidence to the extent that doing so does not interfere with the criminal investigation. In such cases, the head of the investigative agency shall cooperate in the investigation to enable the head of the fire authority to conduct a prompt fire investigation, unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(3) Matters necessary concerning the scope, methods, procedures, etc. of the collection of physical evidence under Article 11 (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Cooperation between Firefighting Officials and Police Officials, etc.)
(1) Firefighting officials and police officials (including autonomous police officials of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province) shall cooperate with each other on the following matters:
1. Matters concerning access to, preservation of, and control of fire scenes;
2. Matters concerning the collection and preservation of physical evidence necessary for fire investigations;
3. Matters concerning obtaining statements from interested persons, etc.;
4. Other matters necessary for fire investigations.
(2) Where the head of a fire authority finds that there are grounds to suspect arson or negligent causing of fire, the head shall notify the police station chief of that fact without delay and cooperate in the criminal investigation, including by collecting and preserving necessary evidence.

Article 13 (Cooperation of Relevant Institutions, etc.)
(1) The heads of fire authorities, the heads of central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, insurance companies, and the heads of other relevant institutions and organizations shall cooperate with each other on matters necessary for fire investigations.
(2) Where necessary to ascertain the cause of a fire, calculate the amount of damage, etc., the head of a fire authority may request the Financial Supervisory Service, relevant insurance companies, etc. to provide insurance enrollment information, etc., including personal information as defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Personal Information Protection Act. In such cases, an institution requested to provide information shall not refuse the request without justifiable grounds.

CHAPTER III PUBLICATION OF FIRE INVESTIGATION RESULTS, ETC.

Article 14 (Publication of Fire Investigation Results)
(1) Where necessary, including to protect the public from suffering damage from similar fires, the head of a fire authority may publish the results of a fire investigation. However, where a criminal investigation is ongoing or is deemed necessary, the head shall consult in advance with the head of the relevant investigative agency on whether to publish the results.
(2) Matters necessary concerning the scope, methods, procedures, etc. of publication under Article 14 (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 15 (Notification of Fire Investigation Results)
The head of a fire authority may notify the heads of central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of other relevant institutions or organizations, or interested persons, etc. of the results of a fire investigation and request that they take necessary measures to prevent similar fires from occurring.

Article 16 (Issuance of Fire Certificates)
(1) Where a person with an interest relating to a fire or a person who needs proof of the details of a fire's occurrence applies for issuance of a document certifying the fire (hereinafter referred to as a "fire certificate" in this Article), the head of a fire authority shall issue the fire certificate.
(2) Matters necessary concerning the procedures and methods for applying for issuance of fire certificates, forms and particulars to be entered, online issuance, etc. shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

CHAPTER IV ESTABLISHMENT OF FOUNDATIONS FOR FIRE INVESTIGATIONS

Article 17 (Designation and Operation of Appraisal Institutions, etc.)
(1) To conduct scientific and professional fire investigations, the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall designate and operate institutions meeting the designation criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as those relating to facilities and specialized personnel, as fire appraisal institutions (hereinafter referred to as "appraisal institutions").
(2) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may provide financial support for all or part of the costs incurred for scientific investigations, analyses, etc. at appraisal institutions designated under Article 17 (1).
(3) Where a person designated as an appraisal institution falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may revoke the designation. However, in the case of subparagraph 1, the Commissioner shall revoke the designation:
1. Where the person obtained the designation by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the person ceases to meet the designation criteria under Article 17 (1);
3. Where the person prepares expert appraisal results inconsistent with the facts, intentionally or through gross negligence;
4. Where the person violates any other requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall hold a hearing before revoking the designation of an appraisal institution under Article 17 (3).
(5) Matters necessary concerning the criteria and procedures for designation of appraisal institutions, revocation of designation, their operation, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Deemed Status as Public Officials for Purposes of Penalty Provisions)
The officers and employees of appraisal institutions designated under Article 17 shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying the penalty provisions of Article 127 and Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 19 (Establishment and Operation of the National Fire Information System)
(1) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall establish and operate a national fire information system that comprehensively collects and manages fire information, including the results of fire investigations, causes of fires, and damage sustained, for use in fire prevention and firefighting activities.
(2) Matters necessary for the collection, management, and use of fire information under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Support for Research and Development Projects)
(1) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may establish policies to support research, experiments, investigations, technological development, etc. necessary for fire investigation techniques (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "research and development projects").
(2) To efficiently promote research and development projects, the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may have an institution, organization, etc. falling under any of the following subparagraphs carry out research and development projects, or may carry out such projects jointly with such institution, organization, etc.: <Amended on January 31, 2025>
1. National or public research institutions;
2. Specific research institutions under Article 2 of the Support of Specific Research Institutions Act;
3. Government-funded research institutions in the field of science and technology established under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes, etc.;
4. Universities, industrial universities, junior colleges, and technical colleges under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
5. Corporations established under the Civil Act or any other Act that are research institutions related to fire investigations or corporate-affiliated research institutes;
6. Corporate-affiliated research institutes or dedicated research and development departments recognized under Article 7 (1) of the Act on Support for Research and Development of Corporate-Affiliated Research Institutes, etc.;
7. Other institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree that conduct research, investigations, technological development, etc. related to fire investigations.
(3) The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may contribute or subsidize all or part of the expenses necessary for institutions, organizations, etc. referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (2) to carry out research and development projects.
(4) Matters necessary for the implementation of research and development projects shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

CHAPTER V PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 21 (Penalty Provisions)
A person who falls under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by a fine not exceeding three million won:
1. A person who moves, alters, or damages objects, etc. at a fire scene without permission, in violation of Article 8 (3);
2. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades entry or an investigation by a fire investigator under Article 9 (1) without justifiable grounds;
3. A person who obstructs the lawful business of an interested person or uses for other purposes or discloses to another person any confidential information learned in the course of conducting a fire investigation, in violation of Article 9 (3);
4. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades the collection of evidence under Article 11 (1) without justifiable grounds.

Article 22 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
If the representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or an individual, commits a violation under Article 21 in connection with the business of the corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to the punishment of the offender: Provided, That this shall not apply if the corporation or individual has not neglected to exercise due care and supervision with respect to the relevant business to prevent such violation.

Article 23 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person who falls under any of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding two million won:
1. A person who enters a controlled area without permission, in violation of Article 8 (2);
2. A person who fails to make a report or submit materials, or makes a false report or submits false materials, in violation of an order under Article 9 (1);
3. A person who, without justifiable grounds, refuses to appear as required under Article 10 (1) or makes a false statement in response to a question.
(2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the head of a fire authority or the police station chief, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 18204, June 8, 2021>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force one year after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (General Transitional Measures)
Dispositions, procedures, and other acts undertaken under the former Framework Act on Firefighting Services as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed to have been undertaken under the corresponding provisions of this Act, if this Act contains provisions corresponding thereto.

Article 3 (Transitional Measures concerning Former Dedicated Investigation Teams)
A dedicated investigation team operated under Article 29 (2) of the former Framework Act on Firefighting Services as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed a dedicated department for fire investigations established and operated under Article 6.

Article 4 (Transitional Measures concerning Persons Previously Qualified to Conduct Fire Investigations)
A firefighting official qualified to conduct fire investigations under Article 29 (2) of the former Framework Act on Firefighting Services as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed a firefighting official qualified as a fire investigator under Article 6 (4).

Article 5 (Transitional Measures concerning Penalties, etc.)
The former provisions shall apply to the application of penalties or administrative fines for violations committed before this Act enters into force.

Article 6 (Amendment to Another Act)
The Framework Act on Firefighting Services is partially amended as follows:

Articles 29 through 33, subparagraph 2 of Article 52, subparagraph 2 of Article 53, and Article 56 (2) 5 shall each be deleted.

Article 7 (Relationship with Other Statutes and Regulations)
If any other statute or regulation cites the former Framework Act on Firefighting Services or any provision thereof as at the time this Act enters into force, and this Act contains a corresponding provision, such citation shall be deemed a citation of this Act or the corresponding provision of this Act in lieu of the former Framework Act on Firefighting Services or the relevant provision thereof.

ADDENDA (Act on Support for Research and Development of Corporate-Affiliated Research Institutes, etc.) <Act No. 20727, January 31, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force one year after the date of its promulgation.

Articles 2 through 5 Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendments to Other Acts)
(1) through (16) Omitted.

(17) The Act on Fire Investigations by Fire Authorities is partially amended as follows:

Article 20 (2) 6 shall be amended as follows:

6. Corporate-affiliated research institutes or dedicated research and development departments recognized under Article 7 (1) of the Act on Support for Research and Development of Corporate-Affiliated Research Institutes, etc.

(18) through (35) Omitted.

Article 7 Omitted.
